gui.main.apps.empty.nohost.title: Add a host to get started
gui.main.apps.empty.nohost.body: A host is the Linux machine your applications run on, as user@address or a name from your ssh config. Waylauncher never stores passwords; it uses your ssh keys and known_hosts.
gui.main.apps.empty.noapps.title: No applications yet
gui.main.apps.empty.noapps.body: Add the first application: a command to run on {host}, such as konsole --separate --nofork.
gui.main.apps.empty.nomatch.title: Nothing matches
gui.main.apps.empty.nomatch.pinned: No applications are pinned. Use “Pin to menu bar” in an application’s ⋯ menu.
gui.main.apps.note.connected: “Connected” means the Waypipe connection is alive. It doesn’t confirm that a window is on screen: Cocoa-Way doesn’t report windows yet.
gui.main.apps.menu.label: More actions for {name}
gui.main.apps.remove.title: Remove {name}?
gui.main.apps.remove.body: This removes the profile from profiles.toml (a backup is kept). Nothing is changed on the host.
gui.main.running.title: Running
gui.main.running.subtitle: {live} active · {ended} ended this session
gui.main.running.empty: Nothing is running. Open an application from Applications.
gui.main.running.note.title: What these states mean.
gui.main.running.note.body: Connecting: pre-launch checks (Cocoa-Way, SSH) are running; only these checks retry. Connected: the Waypipe process is alive. It doesn’t mean a window is visible. Disconnected: the connection ended with an error. The app is never restarted automatically, and Waypipe sessions can’t be reattached: “Start again” launches a new copy. Exited normally also covers waypipe-darwin’s “No child processes” exit after a window close (Settings › Disconnects).
gui.main.running.stop.title: Stop {name}?
gui.main.running.stop.body: This ends {prog} on {host}. Unsaved work in it will be lost. It won’t be restarted.
gui.main.running.detail.select: Select an instance to see its connection details and log.
gui.main.running.detail.window.value: Not reported yet; Focus falls back to bringing Cocoa-Way forward
gui.main.host.title: Hosts
gui.main.host.empty.title: No hosts yet
gui.main.host.empty.body: Add the machine your Linux applications run on.
gui.main.host.checks.title: Connection checks
gui.main.host.checks.none: Nothing has been checked yet. “Run checks” connects once with ssh (BatchMode, no prompts) to test the host key, remote waypipe and the launch wrapper. It doesn’t start any application.
gui.main.host.local.title: Local Network access.
gui.main.host.local.body: macOS doesn’t let apps read this setting. If Terminal reaches the host but Waylauncher reports “No route to host”, check System Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network. Waylauncher never changes it.
gui.main.host.cocoa.window.value: Not available yet: needed for exact window focus (upstream request)
gui.main.host.toast.copied: Copied. Paste it in Terminal to verify the host key.
